Decided (Peter, 2026-08-23): true coordinates are ordinary main-store data. No redaction on load, no private projection of observation_load.

The two stores protect different SUBJECTS. The private store protects participants — tokens, mailing addresses, email — data that exposes a person who did not sign up for it. A taxon-obscured coordinate protects a plant population from collectors, which is a real duty but not participant privacy and does not want the same mechanism. Everyone with access to the main db is trusted to also protect the plants.

Two consequences recorded in ADR 0003: collector locations were never private anyway (collecting for the program implies willingness to say where), so the only secrecy interest in a coordinate is the taxon-driven one; and the control moves from the file to the recipient — 'safe to copy by construction' becomes 'safe to copy to someone trusted', which makes the ADR's own casual example (handing a snapshot to a student) the case that stops being casual. That path wants a derived export with redaction (roadmap phase 7), not a file copy.

Says nothing about REVELATION: whether an atlas may show taxon-obscured coordinates on a label, in the app, or in an export stays per-atlas, open, and a go-live blocker (docs/questions.md).

Diagnosed and fixed. The bead's premise was wrong: the assertion did NOT order by kind and sample_number — test/promote-legacy.test.ts:89 read 'FROM sample ORDER BY kind', so the two trap rows tied on the only ordering key and DuckDB's parallel sort returned them in whichever order the threads finished. That is why it only ever failed under the full suite: solo, the file gets a quieter machine and a stable-looking order. Fix is the missing tie-break (ORDER BY kind, sample_number). Reproduced 2 failures in 8 full-suite runs before; 10/10 green after. Audited every other ORDER BY in test/ — the remaining single-key sorts are over unique columns, and the two other ties (promote-legacy.test.ts:67 determinations, :176 elevations) tie on rows that are identical in every selected column, so a swap is invisible.

Resolving the two routes with coalesce over a LEFT JOIN to specimen rather than a UNION also scans the qc_finding union once instead of twice: on the local 66k-sample store printable_sample went 1.14s -> 0.51s, and the listing roll-up stayed at 0.52s while gaining the specimen route. Regression test in test/listings.test.ts stands a specimen-keyed definition in for one rule view (qc_finding unions rule views by name, so CREATE OR REPLACE on one is enough) and asserts the chip and printability agree; it fails on the old code and passes on the new.

Migration 0007 is a table rebuild, not a rename: DuckDB 1.5.5 refuses ALTER TABLE ... RENAME COLUMN and DROP COLUMN on any table involved in a foreign key, whether or not the column participates, and specimen sits between sample and determination. ADD COLUMN is allowed, which does not help. So specimen and determination are copied out, dropped, recreated verbatim from schema, and copied back with entity_ids preserved, with determination_of_record and the printability chain rebuilt around them. Verified on a copy of the sandbox store: 380,279 / 256,161 / 60,904 / 195,059 identical before and after, entity_id_seq still ahead, no scaffolding left, db:migrate --check clean, applies in under 2s. Re-test the simple rename when DuckDB moves past 1.5.x (beeline-c1b).

Both pages built (the open question answered as 'both', Peter, 2026-08-27).

/specimens/:id: the determination history as events — who, when, which channel, expert or not, the qualifier, verbatim_identification, sex/caste, notes — newest first, with determination_of_record MARKED rather than hoisted, since hoisting it rebuilds the flattened read. Where the record is not the newest the page says why; that is 61,102 specimens on the dev store, so it is the common case rather than an edge.

/samples/:id: the sample in full — collectors in order, dates, method and protocol, place, atlas (with 'no atlas' as an answer), floral host (row absent, not blank, when there was no flower), the observation — plus coordinates with their source provenance and the observation's geoprivacy beside them, elevation with its elevation_source and a stale note, the QC findings in the same words the QC home uses, and a paged list of its specimens. QC findings are sample-keyed, which is why the sample got its own page: on a 2,252-specimen trap sample they would otherwise have been reachable only through one arbitrary specimen. It also gives /samples/:id/edit the parent it never had.

Both pages carry the whole of the other's sample block through shared components (SampleFacts / WhereCollected / SampleFlags), so the two cannot drift into two accounts of one sample.

Gating follows the listings with the filters gone: volunteer reaches their own, staff reach everything, mine follows the acting-for switch, and unreachable answers 404 rather than 403 so a URL cannot be probed. Linked in from both listings and the QC home.

The nineteen LIKE patterns are one regexp_matches alternation. 206 ms -> 16 ms for the predicate; with beeline-2c3.36 the whole qc_finding union goes 518 ms -> 25 ms on the dev store, one sample's findings 24 ms, printable_sample 32 ms. That is the QC home, both listings, printability and both record pages.

Equivalence was measured, not argued: over all 66,065 localities in the dev store (4,539 distinct) the two predicates disagree on NONE, and the rule's output is the same 4,100 rows with an empty symmetric difference — checked before the swap and again after migration 0018 ran against a copy of the store. The reference implementation's own false positives (St Helens, Lane County, Mosier St Park) are reproduced rather than quietly fixed; the space-padded norm supplies the word boundaries, so the alternation is a faithful translation of includesIllegalSuffix and needs no lookbehind.

Recorded in ADR 0001 as a named exception rather than left to be found: regexp_matches is boolean on DuckDB and text[] on Postgres, so a port rewrites this predicate and knows it must. ADR 0001 also now carries the  warning — DuckDB's  is regexp_full_match, Postgres's is partial, and it is the only construct found so far that answers differently in the two engines WITHOUT erroring. beeline-l6w (the portability check) should look for it specifically; that is the reusable finding here.

The old LIKE chain lives on in test/qc.test.ts, run against the new predicate over strings lifted from production staging, so the next edit to the token list has something to disagree with. Two more tests pin every token as a whole word and every near-miss (Drain, Avery Park) as not one.

Wrong premise, and the repo already answered it. A label has six fields (location, coordinates, date, collector, method, field number) and carries no atlas or program name — reference-implementation.md, off LabelsSubtaskHandler.js — so there is no slot for 'whose name'; the collector's name is on it because they collected it, and travelling outside an atlas does not change that. CONTEXT.md already states the handling case positively: assignment to an atlas FOR PROCESSING is an explicit administrative action, so Arizona-through-Washington is handling and is already named as such. Residue is an eventual Ecdysis/GBIF institutionCode, which follows physical custody (OSAC/WSDA) rather than membership, and there is no export to decide it for.
